construct: correlated EXISTS with an unrelated BETWEEN in the same model (column-blind Form-B attribution)
hypothesis: SC-1's Link-B finding: `source_bounds::extract_form_b_bounds` scans the WHOLE model SQL for any `col BETWEEN expr AND expr +/- INTERVAL` pattern and attributes whatever it finds to EVERY source in the BoundContext, ignoring which column/source the match actually belongs to (`_partition_col_upper` param unused). SC-1's own construct happened to have only one such pattern, so the accidental attribution was correct. This cell adds a SECOND unrelated BETWEEN+INTERVAL clause referencing a different source/column (e.g. a WHERE filter on an unrelated payload column) ahead of the real correlated-EXISTS clause in text order, or reorders the true pattern to use `expr - INTERVAL ... AND expr` (lookback form) instead of the lookahead form SC-1 used. Predicted REFUTED = the wrong bound (from the unrelated clause) gets attributed to `conversions`, clamping away the late conversion the same way the original SC-1 hypothesis predicted.

FROM G-08. The exact self-referential-batched-model shape `docs/specs/batched_models.md` documents and `window_independence`'s own unit tests use (a DIRECT join of the driving source to `smelt.<self>`, both exposing the partition column under its OWN name, e.g. `t.d`/`bal.d`) fails at EXECUTION time, not just in maintenance correctness: `crates/smelt-runtime/src/transformer.rs::inject_time_filter` injects the outer output-clamp as a BARE, unqualified `event_time_column` (`format!("{col} >= ... AND {col} < ...")`, no table/alias qualification) whenever the model has more than one bounded source (`is_transparent_single_source` is false for any self-referential model with a nonzero self-margin, since the self-edge is itself a second bounded source). A self-referential model's own driving source and its self-reference both naturally expose a column literally named the partition column (the self table's own materialized schema IS the model's own declared `partition_column`) -- so the direct-join form hits DuckDB `Binder Error: Ambiguous reference to column name` on every run, not merely a wrong-answer divergence. G-08's own test could only proceed by wrapping the self-join in a subquery (`SELECT d, balance FROM (... direct self-join ...) inner_balance`) so the outer clamp's FROM scope exposes only one `d`-named column -- a workaround the spec's own documented pattern does not describe or require. Candidate fix: qualify the injected filter to the specific FROM-item that supplies the model's own output `event_time_column` (the driving/self source, resolved the same way `cumulative.rs`'s `resolve_single_anchor` already picks a driving fact) rather than an unqualified bare column -- OR require/auto-apply the subquery-wrapping this cell discovered is necessary. Recording as its own cell rather than folding into G-08's fix-or-block decision because determining the CORRECT qualification target (which FROM item legitimately owns the output column when several expose the same name) is itself judgment-bearing and deserves its own red-green cell, not a same-iteration side effect.

construct: aggregate event_time (MAX(ts) as projected clock) + timeseries.assert_monotonic
hypothesis: B1 (docs/research/20260707-property-event-time-monotonicity.md §7): MIN(ts)/MAX(ts) as the projected event_time falls into the trace's Undecidable arm (unrecognised function) — the ONLY arm timeseries.assert_monotonic may widen — so a declared model with an aggregate clock is admitted to filter pushdown unsoundly. An aggregate clock is a different property kind (evolution-monotonicity of a group's fold, keyed territory), not an opaque-but-monotone projection: a late row can move a group's MAX(ts) INTO the run window while the group's other contributing rows lie outside the pushed scan, so the folded group is computed from a partial multiset. Expected: REFUTED = bug. Fix shape: classify known aggregate function names as Disproven (or a distinct AggregateClock verdict arm) so the declaration cannot widen them.

construct: stacked window frames across CTEs (7d RANGE inner, 3d RANGE outer)
hypothesis: B2 (docs/research/20260707-property-bounded-reach.md §7, corroborated independently by 20260707-property-filter-distributivity.md §7): BoundResult::merge combines per-construct reaches with MAX, but reach composes in SERIES along a stacked path — a 7d window inside a CTE consumed by a 3d window outside has true backward reach 10d, derived 7d. A row landing 8-10d back is inside true reach but outside the widened scan, so the incremental result diverges from full refresh. Expected: REFUTED = bug. Fix shape: series-add along the operator path, parallel-max only across set-op branches (the tropical-semiring composition), or fail-closed refuse stacked frames until the AST fold exists. RESOLVED 2026-07-07: confirmed and fixed — derive_model_bounds now composes reach through the property walk (series-add via BoundResult::then along nested paths, parallel-max across arms, sibling-slack carry for chained join bands); see ledger SC-4 for the two recorded coverage residues (unparseable-tree fallback to the whole-text scan; same-scope band chains still max-merged).

B6 (docs/research/20260707-property-aggregate-algebra.md §7): discriminants.rs classifies BIT_XOR with needs_inverse: true, contradicting model_maintenance.md rung 3 and keyed_models.md's additive-fold family — BIT_XOR is a self-inverse commutative GROUP (x⊕x = identity), the cheapest retraction of all. Determine which semantics the needs_inverse field actually carries at its consumer sites, fix the drift on whichever side is wrong (code or spec), and add the linkA contract case for self-inverse retraction. Expected: classification drift = bug (direction to be established red-first).

construct: unrecognised function (UDF/opaque) in a skeleton position (partition key / unique key / row membership)
hypothesis: B7 (docs/research/20260707-property-determinism.md §6): the nondeterminism predicate classifies by known function NAME and defaults an unrecognised function to deterministic everywhere except the event-time trace (which is fail-closed via NotTraceable) — so a row-nondeterministic UDF flowing into a partition key, unique key, or WHERE membership predicate passes the taint gate. Replay then mis-addresses rows (double-insert under merge, partition churn under rewrite). Expected: fail-open confirmed = bug. Fix shape: unknown function in a taint-relevant position → fail-closed row-nondeterministic unless allowlisted, mirroring the trace's Undecidable discipline.
